paper_title: Optimal Management Options for Esophageal Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (E-GIST)
study_design: Retrospective single-center descriptive case series with clinician-selected management
evidence_type: Observational treatment-pattern, adverse-event and follow-up evidence
claim: The report describes 23 patients with pathologically confirmed esophageal gastrointestinal stromal tumors at one hospital.
context: Retrospective clinical records from the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University. The total and sex counts agree across the abstract and Table 1; the exact 2023 enrollment cutoff differs between Methods and Results and is not resolved here.
source_locator: Publisher-layout PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 2, Methods 2.1; p. 3, Results 3.1 and Table 1.
scope_does_not_establish: ["Superior safety, survival or oncologic equivalence of endoscopy versus surgery.","A validated universal size cutoff, treatment algorithm or replacement for clinical guidelines.","A causal effect of imatinib or any procedure on recurrence or survival.","Prospective, multicenter or externally validated outcomes.","A reconciled 2023 enrollment cutoff or corrected mitotic-index category."]
limitations: ["The study is retrospective and includes 23 patients at one center. Treatment was chosen by experienced clinicians on the basis of tumor size, location, origin and growth pattern, creating strong selection differences between treatment groups.","No randomized comparison, adjusted treatment-effect estimate or external validation establishes superiority or oncologic equivalence.
